event: Thames Water proposes the Upper Thames Reservoir near Abingdon, described by BBC as 'biggest in 25 years'.
Public inquiry begins into Thames Water's Water Resources Management Plan, examining the Upper Thames Reservoir proposal.
Government rejects the £1bn reservoir following the public inquiry, concluding 'need not proven'.
RAPID (Regulators' Alliance for Progressing Infrastructure Development) gated process for strategic resource options begins, including the South East Strategic Reservoir Option (SESRO).
RAPID gate one final decision published.
Non-statutory consultation opens on interim masterplan and access road options (runs to August 2024).
source_label: Thames Water: White Horse Reservoir project page

event: EIA scoping request submitted to the Planning Inspectorate.
Planning Inspectorate adopts the EIA Scoping Opinion.
Government approves Thames Water's Water Resources Management Plan 2024 (WRMP24), including the White Horse Reservoir.
source_label: Vale of White Horse District Council: SESRO

event: Chancellor Rachel Reeves lists White Horse Reservoir among 'nine new reservoirs' backed by the government, alongside £7.9bn of water resources investment.

Statutory consultation (sections 42/47) opens with the Preliminary Environmental Information (PEI) Report. Nine events held, more than 1,200 attendees and about 2,500 responses by its close on 13 January 2026.
RAPID gate three draft decision published; consultation period opens to 29 January 2026. Decision unlocks up to £100m for further development.
source_label: Ofwat: RAPID gate three draft decision

event: Project renamed White Horse Reservoir. £5.7bn main works contractor tender issued on Find a Tender (notice 005547-2026).
Oxfordshire County Council statutory consultation response submitted; the council says it 'cannot support the application in its current form due to the significant environmental impacts'.
source_label: Ofwat: OCC statutory consultation response (published by Ofwat)

event: Secretary of State issues a section 35 direction letter, published on the Planning Inspectorate's site.
Clay compaction trial summary published by Thames Water.
RAPID confirms gate three passed, clearing the project to proceed towards planning.
source_label: New Civil Engineer: gate three confirmed

event: Thames Water publishes 'community research' findings: 2,004 adults surveyed, 89% said the reservoir is 'important'.
source_label: ITV Meridian: Thames Water polling coverage

event: Pre-application Programme Document published by Thames Water.

Targeted consultation on access points opens (runs to 7 October 2026). Access points raised from 6 to 17. Thames Water acknowledges 'overall construction traffic movements will be higher than previously forecast'.
White Horse Reservoir Growth Coalition launched at a parliamentary event. Led by BusinessLDN and Thames Valley Chamber of Commerce, with eleven founding members.
Three joint ventures shortlisted for the main works contract. Bids expected spring 2027, contract award autumn 2027.
source_label: Smart Water Magazine: joint ventures shortlisted

event: GARD reports that Oxfordshire County Council's submission to the targeted consultation said it 'fails to meet three of the four Gunning Principles' and called for the DCO submission to be delayed.
DCO application submission expected. Not submitted as at 1 November 2026.
RAPID gate four submission planned.
Main construction start (Thames Water website figure). Note: the PEI Report and October 2026 press coverage give 2032 as the main works start date. Both figures are from Thames Water.
First water available. Main works complete approximately 2043.
